findings.title: `getBaseConditions` returns unparenthesized `OR` clauses when `filters` are absent
findings.body: When no filter conditions are set (`filterConditions === null`), `getBaseConditions()` returns `authConditions` directly without outer parentheses. For `org` and `team` scopes, `authConditions` is a top-level `OR` expression (`(A) OR (B)`). If a caller embeds `${baseConditions}` inside a larger `WHERE` clause alongside `AND` conditions (e.g. `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "createdAt" >= ...`), SQL operator precedence binds `AND` tighter than `OR`, evaluating as `(A) OR ((B) AND "createdAt" >= ...)` and leaking unauthorized rows from branch `A` regardless of the additional predicates. `buildFilterConditions` has the same issue when only `eventTypeId` is set (`("eventTypeId" = ...) OR ("eventParentId" = ...)`). Wrap top-level `OR` expressions (or the return value of `getBaseConditions`) in parentheses so they are safe to compose with `AND`.
